# wpbg-hdl spike: can a parent block ever get a `match`? **Verdict: no.** Leaf-only is a permanent ceiling, not a temporary limitation — and not for the reason the ticket gave. `fixMarkup` (Gutenberg's `canonicalize`) recursively re-serializes every descendant whenever it is asked to correct a parent, unconditionally. Whether a given descendant's bytes survive that re-serialization depends entirely on whether the source's existing whitespace/formatting convention happens to already match what the serializer emits for that block type — a property of the input you cannot know without doing the rewrite and diffing the result. That is exactly the "was it corrected or just reformatted?" ambiguity `wpbg-lsf` was built to avoid, so a parent `match` would reintroduce the very problem the feature exists to sidestep. The narrower "wrapper-only defect" rule the ticket's footnote proposed does not hold either — see below. ## What the ticket got wrong (confirmed) The ticket claimed validating a block in isolation strips its children so canonicalizing a parent comes back with them gone. False, and already independently disproven twice before this spike: `wpbg-lsf`'s own implementation report (§3) found `flattenBlockTree` on a canonicalized parent always returns more than one node — children are preserved in the tree, not silently deleted. This spike's probes confirm the same thing from the pipeline side: every nested case below re-parsed with the same child count as its baseline (`invalid-parent-valid-child`: 2→2 blocks; `title.html`: 8→8 in all four probes; `deeply-nested-mismatched-closer`: 4→4; synthetic zero-whitespace: 3→3). Nothing is destroyed. `shallowMarkup()` (which genuinely does strip children, by design, for the unrelated purpose of isolating a block's own verdict) was never the right method to extend for this — there are no child seams to record because full-block canonicalization never loses the children in the first place. ## Method Mirrored `resolveMatch()`'s actual splice exactly (`src/block-locator.js`): original delimiters, `fixMarkup` on the full block markup, `conformToSource(corrected, raw)` on the *whole* canonicalized block before extracting anything, `markupSpan` to pull the trimmed corrected inner element, then splice `slice(node.start, searchSpan.start) + correctedInner + slice(searchSpan.end, node.end)` — but applied to a node with children instead of the leaf-only gate that ships today. `conformToSource` was applied before any byte comparison in every probe (fixtures are CRLF on disk; `fixMarkup` emits LF). Findings were diffed by identity (`block@htmlLine`) against a same-document baseline, and — the decisive check — each descendant's own span was re-located in the candidate document and compared byte-for-byte against its span in the original, not just counted. Probe script: `.scratch/hdl-probe.mjs` (throwaway, not committed). ## Measurements | Fixture | Target | Children | Descendant bytes | Findings delta | |---|---|---|---|---| | `invalid-parent-valid-child.html` | `core/group` L1 | 1 (`core/paragraph`) | **identical** | none | | `title.html` | `core/group` L1 | 3 | **changed** (all 3 children) | resolved-away `core/group@3, core/paragraph@8, core/paragraph@16`; **newly-appeared `core/paragraph@9`** | | `title.html` | `core/group` L6 | 1 | **changed** | resolved-away `core/paragraph@8, core/paragraph@16`; **newly-appeared `core/paragraph@9, core/paragraph@18`** | | `title.html` | `core/group` L14 | 3 | **changed** (2 of 3 children; the `post-title` self-closer is untouched) | resolved-away `core/paragraph@16`; none newly-appeared | | `deeply-nested-mismatched-closer.html` | `core/group` (already clean) | 1 (`core/columns`) | **changed** | resolved-away `core/column@3`; newly-appeared `core/column@2` (a clean parent still gets rewritten and still perturbs child findings) | | synthetic zero-whitespace nested (`.scratch/hdl-nowhitespace.html`) | outer `core/group` | 1 (`core/group`, itself wrapping a valid paragraph) | **changed** (newlines inserted throughout, where the source had none) | none (block-runner still passed) | Block counts never dropped in any probe (always N→N) — confirming the ticket's stated fear is unfounded, independent of everything else in this table. ### Why `invalid-parent-valid-child` looked stable, and why that is not a counterexample This was the one case with byte-identical descendants, and it looked at first like support for a "wrapper-only" class. It is not. I re-ran `fixMarkup` on just that fixture's whole markup and printed the actual output: ``` "\r\n
\r\n\r\n

Hello

\r\n\r\n
\r\n\r\n" ``` The source already had `\r\n

Hello

\r\n` verbatim — that specific fixture happens to already use the exact interior-newline convention Gutenberg's serializer produces for `core/paragraph`. Nothing about the correction being "confined to the wrapper" caused the stability; the coincidence is in the input's own formatting. The synthetic zero-whitespace fixture is the direct test of that claim, and it falsifies it: same shape (outer `core/group` with a wrapper-only class defect, one clean nested child), but built with **no** whitespace anywhere between delimiters and elements. Canonicalizing the outer block **inserted** `\r\n` throughout the inner `core/group` and its paragraph child — bytes the child never had. So byte-preservation is not a function of where the defect lives (wrapper vs. content); it is a function of whether the source's existing convention happens to match what the serializer would produce anyway — which is unknowable in advance and only checkable by doing the rewrite and diffing it. That is already the ambiguity this feature exists to avoid, so it cannot become the test that gates emitting `match`. `deeply-nested-mismatched-closer.html`'s target parent was already clean (`fixMarkup` still produced a rewrite for it) and its child findings still moved — a clean parent isn't even a precondition for the rewrite-collateral problem. ### An independent reason, on its own Two probes (`title.html` L1 and L6) show findings **appearing** that were not present in the baseline (`core/paragraph@9`, `core/paragraph@18`) — not just existing findings moving line, but the reformatted child markup reading as invalid to block-runner where the original did not. A parent `match` would in those cases hand an agent an edit that introduces new invalid blocks it did not have before. That holds regardless of the byte-identity argument above and would be sufficient on its own to rule out parent `match`. ## Does the narrower "wrapper-only" rule hold? No — see above. The ticket's own footnote framed the narrower rule around *where the defect is* ("confined to the parent's opening tag"). That is the wrong axis. Defect location doesn't decide whether descendant bytes survive; the source's pre-existing formatting convention relative to the serializer's own output does, and that is not something inspectable ahead of the rewrite. title: Land or park the in-process block-runner adapter from the bun-inprocess-adapter worktree
description:
The `bun-inprocess-adapter` worktree holds a completed, tested rewrite of
`src/block-runner-adapter.js` that is **not merged** and tracked by nothing. It has stalled
on a goal it cannot reach, but the rewrite itself is independently valuable and at risk of
being lost.

Worktree: `.claude/worktrees/bun-inprocess-adapter` at `f0c8d58`, branch
`bun-inprocess-adapter`, clean tree. Note `.claude/worktrees/` is now gitignored, so the
directory no longer appears in `git status` — this bead is the only thing pointing at it.

## What the worktree contains

`src/block-runner-adapter.js` rewritten from spawning block-runner's CLI as a subprocess to
calling its library API directly (`import { validate, canonicalize } from 'block-runner'`).

- External contract preserved: `validateMarkup()` still returns
  `{ ok, exitCode, data, error, stderr }` and `fixMarkup()` still returns a markup string or
  `null`. No changes were needed in `src/pipeline.js` or `src/cli.js`.
- `exitCode` is synthesized (`report.ok ? 0 : 1`) and `stderr` is always `''`, since a
  library call has neither. Nothing outside the adapter reads either field.
- `canonicalize()` returns the fixed markup on `report.output` — confirmed empirically, not
  just from the `.d.ts`.
- All 37 existing tests pass unmodified, under both Node and plain `bun run`.

Also in the worktree: a `compile` npm script, `bin/*.exe` in `.gitignore`, a README section
on the in-process Layer 2 call, and a `vitest.config.js` comment correction.

Full detail in the worktree's `handoff/2026-09-03-bun-compile-implementation-report.md` and
`handoff/2026-09-03-bun-compile-wp-block-guard-handoff.md`. **Those two files exist only on
that branch** — if it is deleted they go with it, which defeats the purpose `handoff/`
serves.

## Why it stalled

The rewrite existed to make `bun build --compile` viable, and that goal fails for reasons
outside this repo. The compile succeeds (~95 MiB binary) but the binary cannot start, on any
argument including `--help`:

```
error: Cannot find module '../data/patch.json' from 'B:\~BUN\root\wp-block-guard.exe'
```

Root cause: `css-tree@3.2.1` does `createRequire(import.meta.url)` and then
`require('../data/patch.json')`. Bun's `--compile` bundler statically analyzes literal
`require`/`import` calls to decide what to embed in the binary's virtual filesystem, and
cannot see through a runtime-constructed `require`, so `patch.json` is never embedded.
`css-tree` is reached transitively via `block-runner → jsdom → @asamuzakjp/dom-selector →
css-tree`. Fixing it needs a Bun bundler plugin or a patched/pinned `css-tree`, neither
attempted.

Under plain Node and plain `bun run`, everything works. The failure is specific to
`--compile`.

## Why it is worth landing anyway

The adapter rewrite turns out to matter for a reason unrelated to Bun: it makes repeated
block-runner calls essentially free, because the expensive jsdom + `@wordpress/*` boot is
paid once per process instead of once per call. Measured on `develop`'s dependencies:

```
first validate()      8.773s
subsequent validate() 0.014s / 0.011s
canonicalize()        0.012s / 0.022s
```

That is the precondition that makes per-block correction viable, and it invalidates the cost
argument recorded against the `match` field (see wpbg-x8v and
`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md`, amended). The worktree's own report
concluded "no measurable improvement should be claimed on the performance axis" — correct
for a single CLI invocation, which is all it measured, but not for N calls in one process.

## Suggested resolution

1. Decide the disposition of the branch: merge the adapter rewrite into `develop` on its own
   merits, or keep it parked. Merging is the recommendation — it is tested, contract-
   preserving, and unblocks other work.
2. Either way, **copy the two `handoff/` files onto `develop` first** so the investigation
   survives independently of the branch.
3. Separate the Bun-compile goal from the adapter change. The compile blocker is upstream and
   open-ended; it should not hold the rewrite hostage. Split it into its own bead if it is
   still wanted.
4. Do not commit `bin/*.exe`; the worktree already gitignores it.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `handoff/` reports from this worktree exist on `develop`.
- The branch's disposition is decided and recorded — merged, or explicitly parked with a
  reason.
- If merged: the full suite passes on `develop`, and `README.md` describes Layer 2 as an
  in-process library call rather than a CLI spawn.
- The Bun-compile blocker is either tracked separately or explicitly dropped.
close_reason: Merged into develop as 0aed6de. The in-process adapter landed; follow-ups 1effa87 (stderr capture + regression test, 48 tests passing) and ae04887 (README corrections) complete the acceptance criteria. Bun-compile blocker split out to wpbg-0gu; the handoff reports now live on develop via the merge. Measured effect: block-runner's boot is paid once per run instead of once per file.

title: Add verified per-block match text for BLOCK_INVALID under --suggest
description:
Add a `match` field to `BLOCK_INVALID` findings under `--suggest`, carrying the corrected replacement for the finding's `search` text, so an agent can perform a surgical find-and-replace instead of rewriting the whole file. `search` (shipped) is the text to find; `match` is the text to write. Together they are LSP's `TextEdit{range, newText}` expressed as text rather than offsets, which is how the ecosystem models an agent-applicable fix. ## This supersedes wpbg-x8v's rationale `wpbg-x8v` closed this idea as wontfix. **Both of its reasons are now factually out of date** — it is referenced here rather than reopened, since closing it was a deliberate call at the time. | x8v said | Now | |---|---| | "~12s per invalid block, ~48s for that fixture" | **8–32ms per block** after the one-time jsdom boot. That figure was subprocess-era; ADR 0004 moved block-runner in-process. | | "carries an unverified assumption that a block validated in isolation gets the same verdict as in context" | Settled by `wpbg-4n7` / `handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md`, and relied on in production by `src/block-locator.js`. | | "cannot distinguish 'was invalid' from 'was reformatted'" | Sidestepped: the correction is computed per block, not by diffing a whole-document reformat. | x8v's *remaining* true point — that no correction exists for some findings — is handled below by verification rather than by disclaimer. ## Design (probed end to end, works) For each `BLOCK_INVALID` finding whose block is a **leaf** (`children.length === 0`): 1. Take the block's markup — `src/block-locator.js` already computes this span. 2. `corrected = canonicalize(blockMarkup)`. 3. Extract the corrected **inner** content, discarding the corrected delimiters. 4. Build a candidate: the block's **original** delimiters + the corrected inner content. 5. `validate(candidate)`. Clean ⇒ `match` is the corrected inner content. Not clean ⇒ `match: null`. Step 3 is what keeps the edit minimal: `canonicalize` alphabetizes delimiter JSON keys and drops `"layout":{"type":"default"}`, and none of that churn is the defect. For `BLOCK_INVALID` the delimiter is by definition correct — it carries the attributes `save()` is held to — so the repair always belongs on the HTML side. Step 5 is the important one. It makes `match` a **verified** claim: applying it is proven to produce a block that validates. `match: null` then means "no correction exists", not "we didn't try". ### Probe results | Fixture | Block | Result | |---|---|---| | `invalid-heading-missing-class.html` | `core/heading` | `

Hello World

` → `

Hello World

`, splice validates | | `two-invalid-headings.html` | `core/heading` x2 | both corrected, both splices validate | | `title.html` | `core/paragraph` L8, L16 | `style="margin-top:0;..."` added, both splices validate | | `title.html` | `core/group` L1, L6 | parents — `match: null` (see below) | | `unfixable-extra-attribute.html` | `core/group` | correction is byte-identical to the input and the splice **fails** validation ⇒ `match: null`, correctly | That last row is the gate earning its keep: `aria-hidden="true"` is something `save()` will never emit, so no correction exists and the verification step catches it. ## Leaf blocks only, and why A parent block's correction **cannot** be spliced: validation strips inner blocks, so `canonicalize` returns the parent with its children gone. The L1 `core/group` in `title.html` has 3 children and comes back as an empty `
`. Applying that over the block's span silently destroys three blocks. So `match` is `null` for any block with children, unconditionally. Extending to nested blocks needs its own spike — whether a corrected parent still admits its children at the same offsets is an assumption, not a fact. Split that out if it is wanted; do not attempt it inside this bead. ## Line endings are a hard requirement, not a nicety `canonicalize` mangles them. Measured on `title.html` (CRLF throughout): 3 of 4 blocks came back CRLF→LF, and one came back **mixed** — `\n` at the delimiters, `\r\n` retained inside — which is worse than uniform conversion, since a find-and-replace then matches neither. `match` must be normalized to the input file's own line-ending convention before emission. Both the splice candidate in step 4 and the emitted value need this, or step 5 verifies something the agent will not actually apply. ## Scope - Only under `--suggest` (linked bead). Plain `validate` stays a single block-runner call; this costs one extra `canonicalize` + one extra `validate` per invalid leaf block. - `match` sits next to `search` in the finding, after it and before `fix`. - Only `BLOCK_INVALID`. Every other code gets `null` — `STRUCTURAL_*` findings are delimiter defects with no `save()`-derived correction, and the rest have no span at all. ## Acceptance criteria - `match` is `null` for every finding on a plain (non-`--suggest`) run, so the field's presence is stable but the cost is opt-in. - For a leaf `BLOCK_INVALID` with a real correction, replacing `search` with `match` in the source produces a file that validates clean. Assert this by actually performing the replacement and re-running `validateFile`, not by comparing strings. - `match` is `null` for a block with children, and there is a fixture with a nested invalid parent proving no destructive value is emitted. - `match` is `null` for `unfixable-extra-attribute.html`, where the correction does not resolve the finding. - `match`'s line endings match the input file's convention; covered by a CRLF fixture and an LF fixture. - `search` is unchanged by this work.

| Fixture | Working tree | Index |
|---|---|---|
| `wp-block-guard/two-invalid-headings.html` | CRLF x7 | **LF x7** |
| `wp-block-guard/invalid-heading-missing-class.html` | LF x3 | LF x3 |
| `mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` | CRLF x25 | **LF x25** |

`core.autocrlf=true` is set globally on this machine and there is no `.gitattributes`
(`git check-attr text eol` reports `unspecified` for every fixture). So a fixture's
on-disk line endings are a property of the machine and the checkout, not of the repo:

- fresh clone on Windows → **all** fixtures CRLF
- fresh clone on Linux/macOS → **all** fixtures LF

A "CRLF fixture" is therefore a local authoring artifact. An assertion resting on one
would pass here and test nothing on CI.

The line-ending tests **construct** their input byte-by-byte at runtime (joining lines
with an explicit `\r\n` or `\n` and writing the file), so they are immune to
`core.autocrlf` and to platform. `conformToSource` also has direct unit tests for the
normalization rules in isolation. Coverage of the criterion's intent is unchanged; only
the mechanism differs.

No `.gitattributes` was added. Pinning fixture endings repo-wide would renormalize files
and could invalidate line-ending measurements already recorded on other beads — worth its
own ticket if wanted, not a side effect of this one.

`wpbg-lsf` and `wpbg-hdl` both cite `title.html` as "CRLF throughout" and reason from what
canonicalization does to it. **That measurement was taken against a working-tree copy that
is committed as LF.**

not preserve line endings. Measured during this implementation, a CRLF input came back LF
throughout with the trailing newline dropped, which is exactly why `conformToSource`
exists. But the *fixture* will not reproduce it on a fresh clone or on Linux CI, so any
test written for those beads must construct its input the same way rather than reading
`title.html` and assuming CRLF.

# wpbg-lsf: verified per-block `match` text — implementation report Implements the brief for `wpbg-lsf` as given directly (not `br show`, per this session's overrides), following the "Authoritative corrections" section, which supersedes the original ticket body. ## 1. What changed and why `match` is now a field on every finding, populated only for a leaf `BLOCK_INVALID` finding (`node.children.length === 0`) under `--suggest`, and only once the correction has actually been verified to clear the finding. `null` everywhere else, including on every plain (non-`--suggest`) run. ### `src/block-locator.js` - `markupSpan()` stays module-private (see §4 — an earlier pass exported it unnecessarily and that was reverted). - `resolveItemLines()`'s returned entries now carry the block-tree `node` itself alongside the pre-existing `line`/`start`/`end` (the `search` span), instead of discarding it. This is the "widen the return" instruction from correction B: the node is already in hand at the point the span is computed, and `resolveMatch()` needs exactly that node — its `children` to gate leaf-only, its own `start`/`end` to isolate the block for canonicalization. No second tree-walk. - New exported `resolveMatch({ node, searchSpan, sourceContent, raw, fixMarkup, validateMarkup, conformToSource })`: 1. `node.children.length > 0` → `null` immediately, before canonicalization is even attempted (verified as load-bearing, not redundant — see §3). 2. `blockMarkup = sourceContent.slice(node.start, node.end)` — the whole block, original delimiters included, sliced from the *unmasked* source (same source `search` is sliced from). 3. `correctedRaw = await fixMarkup(blockMarkup)` — canonicalize the block alone. `null` output → `null` match. 4. `conformedBlock = conformToSource(correctedRaw, raw)` — conform the **whole** canonicalized block to the file's line-ending convention, *before* extracting the inner span. This order matters and was flagged by the advisor before I wrote the code: `conformToSource` matches `raw`'s trailing-newline state, and `raw` is the whole file, which almost always ends in `\n`. If conform ran *after* extracting the inner span (which has its own surrounding whitespace already trimmed off), the extracted text would read as "lacks a trailing newline" and `conformToSource` would spuriously append one — a blank line an agent's find-and-replace would insert right before the closing delimiter. Conforming the whole block first means that spurious newline lands outside the span that gets extracted next, and is discarded with it. 5. Re-parse `conformedBlock` with the same tokenizer (`buildBlockTree`/ `flattenBlockTree`) used elsewhere in this module, expect exactly one node, and take its `markupSpan()` — the same "trimmed element, delimiters discarded" shape `search` already uses, just applied to the corrected markup instead of the original. This is "extract the corrected inner content" (ticket step 3), expressed as the exact same primitive `search` is built from, not a second extraction mechanism. 6. Splice: `sourceContent` up to the *original* `search` span, plus the corrected inner content, plus `sourceContent` from the end of the `search` span onward — i.e. original delimiters (and any block-internal whitespace outside the trimmed span) plus the corrected element. This is ticket step 4. 7. `validateMarkup(candidate)` and check both `result.ok` (the call itself succeeded) and `(result.data.items || []).length === 0` (the markup is actually valid — `ok` alone is "call succeeded," not "clean"). Clean → return the corrected inner content. Not clean, or the call failed, or the re-parse didn't reduce to one node → `null`. Regarding correction C's "applied to both the splice candidate you validate and the value you emit" — the code calls `conformToSource` exactly **once** (on the whole canonicalized block, per §above), not twice. This was flagged by the Spec review pass and is intentional, not an oversight: the candidate is assembled from the already-conformed inner content plus the original delimiter bytes (which are already native-EOL, being a literal slice of `raw`/`sourceContent`), so the candidate validated is byte-identical to what an agent produces by replacing `search` with `match` in the real file. title: Surface match in the human report alongside search
description:
Surface the `match` field in the human-readable report, alongside `search`.

Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-12, in answer to the open question flagged by both
`wpbg-lsf` (which adds `match`) and `wpbg-dpw` (which adds `search` to human output):
**yes, the human report should display `match`.** This bead exists to carry that out —
neither parent is scoped for it, and neither branch has both halves.

## Why this is its own bead

`match` is added by `wpbg-lsf` in `src/findings.js`. Human rendering lives in
`src/report.js`, rewritten by `wpbg-dpw`. The two were implemented concurrently in
separate worktrees, so neither could see the other's half. This work is only possible
once both have merged to `develop`.

## Baseline once the parents land

`makeFinding()` (`src/findings.js`) will emit keys in this order:

```
code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, search, match, fix
```

`wpbg-dpw`'s approved design renders `search` after the message line and before the
`fix:` line, first-line-only, truncated to a ~80 char cap with a trailing `…`, and omits
the line entirely when `search` is `null`.

## The open design question — resolve before implementing

The obvious move is to render `match` exactly like `search`: a truncated first line,
positioned between them, omitted when `null`. **That may be the wrong default**, and the
reason is worth stating before anyone writes code.

`search` truncated is still useful — it is an *identifier*, and a first line is usually
enough for a human to recognize which block is meant. `match` truncated is **not**
actionable: it is a *payload*, meant to be applied verbatim, and a human cannot copy a
value ending in `…` and use it. Rendering it the same way risks implying an affordance
the output does not provide.

At least three candidate treatments, to be previewed and approved the way `wpbg-dpw`'s
options were:

1. **Symmetric with `search`** — `match: <first line>…`. Consistent, but see above.
2. **Presence indicator only** — e.g. a `(fix available)` marker or a distinct color on
   the finding's marker when `match` is non-null, with the value itself left to `--json`.
   Treats "a verified correction exists" as the signal a human actually needs, and keeps
   the human report readable, which is the complaint `wpbg-dpw` exists to answer.
3. **Full untruncated value** — accurate and copy-pasteable, but `match` can be a
   20+ line markup blob, which reintroduces exactly the unreadability `wpbg-dpw` fixed.

Option 2 is the recommendation; do not treat that as decided.

## Semantics that must survive whichever option wins

`match: null` is load-bearing and must not read as an error or an omission. Per
`wpbg-lsf`, `null` means one of three distinct things, all legitimate:

- the finding is not `BLOCK_INVALID`;
- the block has children (leaf-only is the current ceiling, see `wpbg-hdl`);
- a correction was computed and **failed verification**, i.e. no correction exists.

The human output should not imply the tool failed to try. Note also that `match` is only
populated under `--suggest`, so a plain run shows nothing regardless — the rendering must
not look broken in the common case.

## Acceptance criteria

- A proposal with previews built from real CLI output has been presented to and approved
  by the maintainer.
- Implementation matches the approved option.
- Behaviour under a plain (non-`--suggest`) run is covered by a test: no `match` surface
  appears, and the output does not regress.
- `match: null` under `--suggest` renders per the approved option without implying failure.
- Colorization follows `wpbg-dpw`'s established scheme and suppression rules (non-TTY,
  `--json`, `NO_COLOR`); no new dependency.
- `search` rendering is unchanged by this work.

## Closing as `wontfix` — the premise was wrong, confirmed by the maintainer

This bead asked whether the human report should display `match`. The approved answer was

Confirmed with the maintainer: *"only the agent with `--json` would ask for suggestion, in
order to fix a fragment of code."* `--suggest` is the **agent** workflow

`--suggest`-requires-`--json` rule is a deliberate boundary between the two, and the earlier
plan to relax it so this feature could render would have inverted a design decision in order
to justify a feature that existed only because of a misreading.

`match` belongs to the JSON contract only. There is no human rendering of it, and a future
proposal to add one should be treated as a request to change the `--suggest`/`--json`
boundary first — which is the real decision, and a much larger one than a report line.

An implementation was completed on branch `wpbg-n9u` (146/146 passing, `src/report.js` +
`tests/report.test.js`) before the unreachability was found. The tests passed because they
call `formatHuman()` directly with a constructed report — correct unit tests of code the CLI
cannot reach. **The branch has been discarded.** Nothing was merged to `develop`.

The defect was in this bead's brief, not in the implementation: the brief asserted the line
would render, so neither the implementer, its two code-review sub-agents, nor its advisor had
reason to question reachability.

`wpbg-ztf` (ADR 0003 + `CONTEXT.md` amendments for `match`) must record that `match` is
JSON-only and never appears in human output — otherwise this idea will be re-proposed the
next time someone reads the finding schema. That has been added to its scope.

title: CLI fails to match files on Windows-style backslash paths
description:
On Windows, running the CLI with a backslash-style path (e.g. .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html) fails with "No matching .html or .php files found for: ..." even though the file exists.

Root cause: src/cli.js:66 passes raw argv patterns directly into fast-glob (fg). fast-glob treats backslash as a glob escape character, not a path separator, so a pattern like .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html gets mangled into .\tests\fixturesmastermind-lsparts\footer.html (backslash + following char is consumed as an escape sequence) and never matches.

Repro (confirmed):
- fg([".\\tests\\fixtures\\mastermind-ls\\parts\\footer.html"]) -> []
- fg(["./tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/footer.html"]) -> matches correctly

Reported via: `npm start .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` and `npx . .\tests\fixtures\mastermind-ls\parts\footer.html` both failing.

Suggested fix: normalize backslashes to forward slashes on each pattern before passing to fast-glob in src/cli.js, so Windows-style paths are supported.

(Recreated from firecrawl-cli-g1c after fixing the workspace's issue_prefix config from firecrawl-cli to wpbg.)

title: Add search field to finding schema carrying byte-exact source text
description:
Add a `search` field to the finding schema carrying the **byte-exact source text** of the flagged markup, so an agent-facing (JSON) consumer can locate what to replace without re-deriving positions from prose. `fix` is unchanged — it stays advisory prose for the human operator. `match` (the corrected replacement text) is **out of scope** and tracked separately as wontfix; see "Why `match` is not here" below. ## Field order In `makeFinding()` (`src/findings.js`), the returned object gains one field, `search`, positioned after `message`, before `fix`: ```js { code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, search, fix } ``` ## What `search` contains, per finding code | Code | `search` | |---|---| | `PHP_HEADER_STRIPPED` | the stripped `` header text | | `PHP_INTERPOLATION_UNCHECKED` | the exact matched `` fragment (captured before `maskEmbeddedPhp` blanks it) | | `STRUCTURAL_UNBALANCED_DELIMITER`, `STRUCTURAL_MISMATCHED_CLOSER`, `STRUCTURAL_INVALID_ATTRS_JSON` | the exact delimiter comment text (``), sliced from the token's byte offsets already computed in `tokenizeDelimiters()` (`src/structural.js`) | | `BLOCK_INVALID`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING` | **`null`** — see "block-runner positions are not usable" below | | `BLOCK_RUNNER_SKIPPED`, `BLOCK_RUNNER_FAILURE`, `STRUCTURAL_NO_BLOCKS` | `null` — no single location to point at | Everything `search` is populated for comes from **our own tokenizer**, never from block-runner. That is the whole reason this bead is cheap: no extra subprocess, no headless-Gutenberg boot, no dependency on block-runner's source mapping. ## block-runner positions are not usable (verified) The original version of this bead specified `search` for `BLOCK_INVALID` / `BLOCK_RUNNER_WARNING` as "the single source line at `item.source.htmlLine`". That was investigated against `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` and **does not work**, for two independent reasons: 1. **`htmlLine` points at the delimiter comment, never the faulty element.** For all four `BLOCK_INVALID` findings on that fixture, the text needing replacement is the `
`/`

` on the *following* line. Slicing at `htmlLine` yields the `` comment, which is not what is at fault. 2. **Positions are misattributed.** Finding #2 reports `htmlLine: 3` / `offset: 183`, which is the `hero-blob-1` group — confirmed **valid** when validated in isolation — while its `reason` describes the `word-cloud-bg` group at line 6. block-runner appears to map the nth finding of a block name to the nth occurrence of that name in document order, skipping the valid ones. Tracked as its own bug (see linked bead). Emitting a `search` value derived from those positions would hand an agent the wrong text to find and replace, which is worse than emitting nothing. Hence `null` for both codes until the position bug is resolved. ## Why `match` is not here Producing corrected markup requires running the block's `save()` function. WordPress/Gutenberg PR #82013 ("Try: declare block transforms in block.json, read them in the editor and in PHP", open, unmerged, `lib/experimental/`) states this directly in its "What this does not solve" section: > Producing saved markup is a separate problem […] Turning attributes into markup means > running the block's `save()`, which only exists in JavaScript. Empirically confirmed against block-runner: - `validate --json` reports the diff only as prose in `reason` ("Expected attributes [ … ], instead saw [ … ]") — a normalized attribute-tuple diff with no tag name, no quoting and no attribute order. It cannot be turned into replacement text. `--explain` adds nothing to the JSON. - The only real HTML pair ("Content generated by `save` function" / "Content retrieved from post body") appears on **`fix`'s stderr**, for **one** block per run, and only for blocks `fix` could not repair. `validate` writes nothing to stderr. - `fix` reformats the entire document (strips indentation, reorders delimiter JSON keys, drops `"layout":{"type":"default"}`), so a pre/post diff cannot distinguish "was invalid" from "was reformatted" — the verified-valid `hero-blob-1` block changes too. - Some blocks have no `save()`-compatible correction at all (`aria-hidden="true"` on a `core/group`). Upstream's own answer to this is to let a block *declare* it cannot round trip (`serverConversion: false`), not to produce a fix. The only viable route is extracting each block and running `save()` on it one at a time — roughly 12s per invalid block, ~48s for that one fixture. Rejected as disproportionate. ## Touch points - `src/findings.js` — add `search` to the returned object and to `makeFinding()`'s JSDoc, defaulting to `null` when not supplied. - `src/structural.js` — `checkStructuralBalance()` must pass through each token's `start`/`end` on the findings it emits. **Keep its signature unchanged** (it is exported and tested with tokens only); let `runStructuralLayer()`, which already has `content`, do the slicing. - `src/php-fragment.js` — `scanForEmbeddedPhp()` must return the matched fragment text. **Add** a field rather than renaming `token`; `tests/php-fragment.test.js` asserts on `occurrences[0].token`. For an unterminated opener (the fallback loop, no matching `?>` before EOF) there is no fragment to slice — emit the opener text. - `src/pipeline.js` — thread `search` into each `makeFinding()` call. Slice from the **pre-mask** body: structural tokenization runs on the masked body, and `maskEmbeddedPhp` blanks PHP to spaces, so slicing from it is not byte-exact. Masking is length-preserving, so offsets are identical — keep a reference to the body before masking and slice `search` from that. - `src/cli.js` — the per-file `catch` block hand-builds a `BLOCK_RUNNER_FAILURE` finding object, bypassing `makeFinding()`. Either route it through `makeFinding()` or add `search: null` so every finding in the output has the same shape. ## Out of scope - `--json` output (`src/cli.js`) picks `search` up automatically once `makeFinding()` returns it — no separate change needed. - `formatHuman()` (`src/report.js`) is **not** touched here. Surfacing `search` in the human report belongs to the colorized/tabular report bead, which is gated on a rendering proposal. - `--fix`'s current write-the-file behaviour is unchanged by this bead. ## Acceptance criteria - Every finding code in the table above produces the specified `search` value (or `null`) in `--json` output. - `search` text is byte-exact from the file content, sliced from the pre-mask body (no re-indenting or trimming). - Every finding in `--json` output has a `search` key, including the one built by hand in `src/cli.js`'s catch block. - `checkStructuralBalance()`'s signature is unchanged; `scanForEmbeddedPhp()` still returns `token`. - Existing tests pass. Note `tests/structural.test.js` asserts `toEqual([{ code: 'STRUCTURAL_NO_BLOCKS', line: 1 }])` — the one exact-object assertion that adding fields to structural findings will break; update it. Everything else uses `toMatchObject` / `objectContaining` and survives. - Add fixtures covering `search` for **each** populated code — `PHP_HEADER_STRIPPED`, `PHP_INTERPOLATION_UNCHECKED`, and at least one of the three `STRUCTURAL_*` codes — plus one asserting `BLOCK_INVALID` yields `search: null`. - Add a fixture with embedded PHP **inside a delimiter comment's attribute JSON**. This is the only case where slicing from the masked body differs from the pre-mask body, so it is the only test that can catch the pre-mask instruction being ignored. Without it that requirement is unenforced. ## Known limitation of this bead as scoped `BLOCK_INVALID` is the code that fires on real input (all four findings on `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` are `BLOCK_INVALID`), and it yields `search: null` here because block-runner's positions cannot be trusted — see the linked position bug. So on the markup that motivated this work, the new field is entirely `null`. That is deliberate: emitting text derived from a misattributed position would hand an agent the wrong thing to replace. Visible value for `BLOCK_INVALID` arrives only once the position bug is fixed.
close_reason: search implemented across all finding codes; BLOCK_INVALID populated from block-locator spans (wpbg-djb having removed the blocker), ADR 0002 amended. 78 tests passing.

title: resolveMatch docstring states a mechanism wpbg-hdl disproved
description:
`resolveMatch()`'s docstring in `src/block-locator.js` (around lines 171-178) states a
mechanism that `wpbg-hdl` proved false. The gate it describes is correct and must stay; only
its stated reason is wrong.

## Current text

> `null` for a block with children, unconditionally: validating a block in isolation strips
> its inner blocks (see `shallowMarkup()` above), so **canonicalizing a parent comes back with
> its children gone**, and splicing that in would silently destroy them.

## Why that is wrong

Canonicalizing a parent's **full** markup preserves its children completely — measured three
independent times (`wpbg-lsf` implementation report §3, the `wpbg-hdl` triage probes, and the
`wpbg-hdl` spike itself; every nested probe re-parsed with an unchanged block count, N→N).

The "children gone" behaviour belongs to `shallowMarkup()`, which strips children **by design**
for the unrelated purpose of isolating a block's own verdict. The docstring conflates the two
operations — which is exactly the confusion that sent `wpbg-hdl`'s original brief down a
seam-recording method that was never needed.

## The real reason, per the spike

`fixMarkup` recursively re-serializes every descendant when correcting a parent. Whether a
descendant's bytes survive depends on whether the source's existing whitespace convention
already matches what the serializer emits — not on where the defect is. That is unknowable
without performing the rewrite and diffing it, which is the "was it corrected or just
reformatted?" ambiguity `match` exists to avoid. In two probes the rewrite also *introduced*
findings absent from the baseline.

Full reasoning: `handoff/2026-09-12-wpbg-hdl-spike-findings.md` and the 2026-09-12 amendment in
`docs/adr/0002-search-is-byte-exact-or-absent.md`.

## Scope

- Rewrite the docstring's justification to state the real mechanism and point at ADR 0002's
  2026-09-12 amendment.
- Say plainly that leaf-only is **permanent**, not a temporary ceiling — the current text's
  "Nested-parent support is out of scope here (wpbg-hdl)" reads as deferral, and `wpbg-hdl` is
  now closed with a settled "no".
- **Comment-only change. No behaviour change.** The `node.children.length > 0` gate stays
  exactly as it is.

## Acceptance criteria

- The docstring no longer claims canonicalization strips children.
- It states the re-serialization reason and cites ADR 0002's amendment.
- Leaf-only reads as a settled decision rather than a pending limitation.
- Full suite still passes (157/157 baseline); no source behaviour changed.

whitespace inside its docstring. Confirmed by `git diff --stat`: every changed line is a
`*`-prefixed comment line in `src/block-locator.js`, plus one comment line in a test file
(see below) — no code line, no assertion, no test body changed.

## What was wrong

`resolveMatch()`'s docstring said:

> `null` for a block with children, unconditionally: validating a block in isolation
> strips its inner blocks (see `shallowMarkup()` above), so canonicalizing a parent comes
> back with its children gone, and splicing that in would silently destroy them.
> Nested-parent support is out of scope here (wpbg-hdl).

Two things were false, per the sources this ticket asked me to read against the code:

1. **The mechanism.** Canonicalizing a parent's full markup does not strip its children —
   `flattenBlockTree` on the canonicalized result always comes back with the same block

 * `null` for a block with children, unconditionally: validating a block in
 * isolation strips its inner blocks (see `shallowMarkup()` above), so
 * canonicalizing a parent comes back with its children gone, and splicing
 * that in would silently destroy them. Nested-parent support is out of scope
 * here (wpbg-hdl).
```

```
 * `null` for a block with children, unconditionally — a settled ceiling
 * (wpbg-hdl), not a pending limitation. Canonicalizing a parent does not
 * strip its children (that is `shallowMarkup()` above, for the unrelated
 * purpose of isolating a *verdict*); it recursively re-serializes every
 * descendant, the way Gutenberg's `canonicalize`/`save()` does for any markup

 * formatting already matches what the serializer would emit for that block

 * the rewrite and diffing it, the exact ambiguity `match` exists to avoid
 * answering by inspection. So a parent's `match` would be a bulk,

title: Assess block-runner 0.9.7: what 0.9.x added, and whether to upgrade now
description:
`block-runner` has moved 0.8.0 → 0.9.7 while this repo has stayed on 0.8.0. Fourteen releases
landed between 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-15 (0.9.0 through 0.9.7 in six days). This ticket is the
investigation: work out what 0.9.x actually added, whether any of it is useful here, and whether
to upgrade now or deliberately stay put.

## What is already known (gathered 2026-09-17, read-only, nothing installed)

### The WordPress tree does not move with it

This was the original reason for looking. It turns out to be a dead end, and that is worth
recording so nobody re-runs the check:

| Pinned by block-runner | 0.8.0 | 0.9.7 | npm `latest` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@wordpress/block-editor` | 17.0.0 | 17.0.0 | 17.1.0 |
| `@wordpress/block-library` | 10.5.0 | 10.5.0 | 11.0.0 |
| `@wordpress/blocks` | 15.27.0 | 15.27.0 | 16.0.0 |
| `jsdom` | 29.1.1 | 29.1.1 | — |

block-runner pins these **exactly**, not as ranges. Upgrading it brings no newer WordPress
packages. Upstream has since shipped a `block-library` major and a `blocks` major, but reaching
them requires block-runner to adopt them first. Overriding its pins from here would run headless
Gutenberg against a combination block-runner has never tested.

Corollary for `wpbg-0gu`: 0.9.7 still pins jsdom 29.1.1, so the css-tree `createRequire` chain is
unchanged and a block-runner bump would **not** unpark the bun `--compile` failure.

### The API surface this repo consumes appears unchanged

Checked by extracting the 0.9.7 tarball and diffing its `dist/index.d.ts` against the installed
0.8.0:

- `validate(markup, options?)` and `canonicalize(markup, options?)` → `Promise<BlockRunnerReport>`:
  identical signatures. These are what `src/block-runner-adapter.js` imports.
- Every field the pipeline reads — `ok`, `summary.blocks`, `items`, `output` — unchanged.
  `BlockRunnerReport` and `ReportItem` only *gain* optional fields (`source?`, `evidence?`,
  `code?`).
- The 0.9.x changelog lists no removals or breaking changes on the validate path.

### What 0.9.x actually added

A large, essentially self-contained registered-block **authoring** workflow: `author <html>`,
`plugin inspect|preview|write`, source-bound semantic proposals, a `GeneratedAuthoringPlan`,
native style adapters, licensed font transport, pattern-override support. That is why the
dependency list grows by `@babel/parser`, `php-parser`, `postcss`, `ajv`, and `react`/`react-dom`,
and why `wesper` moves 0.0.2 → 0.4.1. `commander` is *downgraded* 15 → 14 deliberately, to keep
the Node 20 line supported.

None of that is on this tool's path today — but whether any of it *should* be is part of the
assessment, not a foregone conclusion.

## The actual cost: `engines`

block-runner 0.9.7 declares `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24.0.0`, narrower than this package's
declared `>=20`. It is a **runtime** dependency of a published `bin` package, so adopting it
without amending `engines` in `package.json` silently breaks consumers on Node 20.0–20.18 and
22.0–22.12. The upgrade is therefore not a one-line version bump; it is a bump plus a deliberate,
documented narrowing of this package's own support contract.

## Open questions this ticket must answer

1. Does `captureStderr()` still behave under 0.9.7? It patches a global (ADR 0004) and its
   soundness depends on block-runner's stderr behaviour. A type diff cannot answer this — it
   needs a real run against the existing suite.
2. Does 0.9.x's new `php-parser` dependency overlap this repo's own PHP-fragment flagging layer?
   Possible duplication, possibly a better upstream implementation to defer to. Treat as a
   question, not a finding.
3. Is any 0.9.x capability worth adopting here, or is the authoring workflow simply out of scope
   for a pre-publish validator? A clear "no, and here is why" is a perfectly good outcome.
4. Do the fourteen releases in six days suggest waiting for the churn to settle?

## Acceptance criteria

- A recommendation is recorded: upgrade now, upgrade later with a stated trigger, or stay on
  0.8.0 with a stated reason. Any of the three is a valid result.
- If the recommendation is to upgrade: the suite passes against 0.9.7, `captureStderr()` is
  verified by a real run rather than inspection, and `engines` in `package.json` is amended in
  the same change with a comment explaining the narrowing.
- If the recommendation is to stay: the reason is recorded where the next person to notice the
  version gap will find it, so this investigation is not repeated from scratch.
- Question 2 (php-parser overlap) is answered either way, since it bears on this repo's own
  PHP layer regardless of the upgrade decision.

## Out of scope

- Upgrading vitest 4 → 5. Separate concern, devDependency only, and it touches `vitest.config.js`.
- Bumping `@wordpress/*` directly by overriding block-runner's pins.
- Adopting the authoring/plugin workflow itself. If the assessment says it is worth having, that
  is its own ticket.

title: Add match field carrying corrected replacement markup
description:
Add a `match` field to the finding schema carrying the **corrected replacement markup**
for a flagged block, so an agent could perform a find-and-replace using `search` (see
linked bead) as the text to find and `match` as the text to write, without the CLI
editing any file.

Recorded and closed as **wontfix**. The reasoning is below so it does not have to be
rediscovered; reopen if the upstream situation changes.

## Why this cannot be done cheaply

Producing corrected block markup means running the block's `save()` function.
WordPress/Gutenberg PR #82013 ("Try: declare block transforms in block.json, read them in
the editor and in PHP" — open, unmerged, `lib/experimental/`) says so directly in its
"What this does not solve" section:

> Producing saved markup is a separate problem […] Turning attributes into markup means
> running the block's `save()`, which only exists in JavaScript.

<https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/82013>
Parent issue: <https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/issues/13163>

That upstream work is about HTML→blocks *conversion*, not validation diffs, and is not
usable today in any case. See also
`archive/2026-09-02-wordpress-gutenberg-markup-validation-research.md`.

## What was ruled out empirically

Investigated against `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html` (4 `BLOCK_INVALID`
findings):

1. **Parsing `reason` from `validate --json`.** The diff is present but only as prose —
   "Expected attributes [ [ 'class', … , true ] ], instead saw [ … ]". It is a normalized
   attribute-tuple diff with no tag name, no quoting style and no attribute order, so it
   cannot be turned into replacement markup. `--explain` adds nothing to the JSON.

2. **Scraping the real HTML pair from `fix`.** `fix` does emit genuine markup on
   **stderr** — "Content generated by `save` function" (the correction) and "Content
   retrieved from post body" (the original). But it emits it for **one** block per run,
   and only for a block it could *not* repair. `validate` writes nothing to stderr at all.

3. **Diffing pre/post canonicalization in memory.** `fix` without `--out` is
   non-mutating (input checksum verified unchanged) and prints corrected markup to stdout,
   which looked promising. But it reformats the **entire** document — strips indentation,
   reorders delimiter JSON keys, drops `"layout":{"type":"default"}`, inserts blank lines.
   The verified-valid `hero-blob-1` block changes too, so "changed == was invalid" is
   false and the diff produces spurious pairs.

4. **No correction exists for some blocks.** `aria-hidden="true"` on a `core/group`
   survived `fix` because `save()` will never emit it. Upstream's own answer to this class
   of problem is to let a block *declare* that it cannot round-trip
   (`serverConversion: false`, or `{ "requires": … }`), not to generate a fix. So `match`
   would legitimately be `null` for an unbounded set of real findings.

## The only viable route, and its cost

Extract each block with our own tokenizer and run block-runner on it one block at a time.
That sidesteps the position-misattribution bug (we choose what we send) and gives
element-level, non-overlapping replacements. Cost is roughly 12s per invalid block — about
48s for that single fixture — and it carries an unverified assumption that a block
validated in isolation gets the same verdict as in context, which is doubtful for deeply
nested blocks whose parents are also invalid.

Rejected as disproportionate to the value.

## If this is reopened

- `search` (linked bead) already gives an agent byte-exact text to locate; a human or LLM
  supplying the correction covers most of the original intent without this field.
- The position-misattribution bug (linked bead) must be fixed first — per-block extraction
  needs a trustworthy mapping from a block-runner finding to one of our tokens.
- Check whether block-runner has since gained a structured expected/actual pair in its
  `validate --json` report; that would collapse this to a cheap change.
close_reason: Wontfix: producing corrected markup requires running the block's save(), which only exists in JavaScript (Gutenberg PR #82013). Rationale recorded in docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md; reopen if block-runner gains a structured expected/actual pair.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Correction to this bead's close reason (2026-09-04)

The close reason on this bead states that per-block canonicalization costs "~12s per
invalid block (~48s for one fixture)" and rejects it as disproportionate. **That figure is
wrong as a general claim**, and cost should not be cited as a reason to keep this closed.

The 12s was measured against `src/block-runner-adapter.js` as it stands on `develop`, which
spawns a fresh block-runner process per call and therefore re-pays the jsdom +
`@wordpress/*` boot every time. Called in-process, the boot happens once:

```
first validate()       8.773s
subsequent validate()  0.014s / 0.011s
canonicalize()         0.012s / 0.022s
```

Per-block correction across a whole file is therefore fractions of a second on top of the
validation the tool already performs — conditional on the adapter calling block-runner as a
library rather than spawning it. That rewrite exists, tested, in the
`bun-inprocess-adapter` worktree; see wpbg-km9, now linked as a blocker.

`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md` has been amended accordingly.

## What still justifies keeping this closed

The correctness objections are untouched:

- block-runner exposes no per-block correction; `reason` is a normalized attribute-tuple
  diff, not swappable text; `fix`'s stderr yields one pair per run; whole-document
  canonicalization reformats valid blocks, so the pre/post diff route stays dead.
- Some blocks have no `save()`-compatible correction at all (`aria-hidden` on a
  `core/group`), so `match` would be `null` for a real share of findings.
- **Unverified and the actual blocker:** whether a block validated in isolation gets the
  same verdict as in context. Most doubtful for deeply nested blocks whose parents are also
  invalid. Settle this before reopening.

Also note the `save()`-is-JavaScript-only argument was over-weighted originally: it rules
out PHP/server-side routes, which is what Gutenberg PR #82013 concerns, but this tool
already runs `save()` through block-runner in jsdom.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Reopened — the blocking spike (wpbg-4n7) came back "sound"

Reopened per `wpbg-4n7`'s acceptance criteria, which specified reopening this bead if
block isolation turned out to be sound. It is.

### What was settled

A block sliced at its exact delimiter span and validated alone gets the same verdict and
reason as it does in its document — verified on 18 blocks across two fixtures with 0
divergences, and true *by construction*: `validateBlock` compares
`getSaveContent(blockType, block.attributes)` against `block.originalContent`, and `save()`
receives no block context. Nothing outside a block's own span feeds its validation.

Full detail: `handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md`.

### Cost figures (the original objection, now dead)

The ~12s-per-block estimate that justified closing this bead was measured before the
in-process adapter (`wpbg-km9`). Re-measured in one process:

| operation | cost |
|---|---|
| first call (jsdom + Gutenberg boot) | ~7.9s, paid once per process regardless |
| isolated `validate()` per block | median 9ms / 2ms across two fixtures; 8 blocks = 128ms total |
| isolated `canonicalize()` per block | 12ms and 34ms on the two repairable blocks tested |

Canonicalizing every invalid block in a file is fractions of a second, not ~48s.

### Per-block canonicalize actually works

Three invalid blocks from `tests/fixtures/mastermind-ls/parts/title.html`, canonicalized
alone:

| block | result |
|---|---|
| `core/paragraph` line 8 | **repaired**, 34ms — `style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:0"` added; summary `1 valid, 0 invalid` |
| `core/paragraph` line 16 | **repaired**, 12ms — `style="margin-top:0;margin-bottom:1.25rem"` added |
| `core/group` line 6 | **not repaired** — `aria-hidden="true"` has no attribute to hold it |

Critically, the whole-document reformatting problem that made a pre/post diff useless
**disappears when the input is a single block**: there are no untouched sibling blocks to
be reindented, so the output is the corrected block and nothing else.

### Two new obstacles, neither known when this was closed

1. **Canonicalize is not byte-preserving.** The line-8 paragraph's numeric character
   references (`你好` and friends) came back as literal CJK/Cyrillic/Greek
   characters. Semantically equivalent; still a rewrite of content the user did not ask to
   change. A `match` field would need to either accept this or re-encode.
2. **Not every invalid block is repairable.** The `aria-hidden` group is the known case.
   `match` must be `null` for those, and the schema needs to distinguish "no correction
   exists" from "correction not attempted".

### Not yet decided

Whether `match` is worth having at all is still a design call — this bead is reopened
because its *stated blocker* is resolved, not because the feature has been re-approved.
`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md` needs revisiting either way: its
cost-based reasoning is superseded, and the two obstacles above are what actually remain.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
## Rationale superseded (2026-09-05) — see wpbg-lsf

This bead's cost and feasibility reasoning is now out of date. Recording it here so a
future reader does not act on the numbers above. Left closed deliberately — the close was
the right call on the day, and wpbg-lsf carries the work under a narrower scope.

- **"~12s per invalid block, ~48s for that fixture"** — measured in the subprocess era.
  ADR 0004 moved block-runner in-process; per-block `canonicalize` + `validate` now costs
  **8–32ms** after the one-time jsdom boot.
- **"an unverified assumption that a block validated in isolation gets the same verdict as
  in context"** — settled by wpbg-4n7 and `handoff/2026-09-05-block-isolation-verdict-spike.md`,
  and now relied on in production by `src/block-locator.js`.
- **"the position-misattribution bug must be fixed first"** — done, wpbg-djb.
- **"a pre/post diff cannot distinguish 'was invalid' from 'was reformatted'"** — still
  true of the whole-document diff, and sidestepped in wpbg-lsf by computing the correction
  per block and verifying it by re-validation rather than by diffing.

What remains true is that no correction exists for some findings — `aria-hidden="true"` on
a `core/group` is still unfixable. wpbg-lsf handles that by *proving* it per finding
(splice the candidate, re-validate, emit `null` when it does not resolve) rather than by
declining to emit the field.

title: Amend ADR 0003 and CONTEXT.md for the new match field
description:
Amend the docs that `wpbg-lsf` made factually false by adding the `match` field.

`wpbg-lsf` (closed, merged as `d4b40cd`) added a verified `match` field to
`BLOCK_INVALID` findings under `--suggest`. Two documents still describe the world as it
was before that landed. Both were deliberately left untouched by the implementer so the
change would be a documentation decision rather than a side effect of a code ticket.

## 1. `docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md`

Its status line is **now false**. The ADR is framed as a live prohibition on putting
corrected markup in findings, and `match` is exactly that — corrected markup, in a
finding.

The ADR should not simply be deleted or flipped to "superseded" without carrying its
reasoning forward. Its original objection was sound and is the reason `match` is built
the way it is: an *unverified* correction in a finding is a liability, because a consumer
cannot tell a real fix from a guess. `wpbg-lsf` did not overturn that objection — it
satisfied it, by re-validating every splice before emitting it and returning `null` when
verification fails. The amendment should say so, so the constraint survives as a design
rule rather than reading as a rule that was simply abandoned.

Note also that `docs/adr/0002-search-is-byte-exact-or-absent.md` states the same honesty
principle for `search` and remains accurate; 0003's amendment should be consistent with
it.

## 2. `CONTEXT.md` glossary

Has no `match` entry, unlike every other agent-facing finding field (`search`,
`Suggestion`, `fixSkippedReason`). Add one.

The entry needs to carry the three distinct meanings of `match: null`, since they are not
interchangeable and the distinction is load-bearing for consumers:

- the finding is not `BLOCK_INVALID`;
- the block has children (leaf-only is the current ceiling — see `wpbg-hdl`);
- a correction was computed and **failed verification**, i.e. no correction exists.

It should also record that `match` is only populated under `--suggest`, and that it is
additionally suppressed when the file contains embedded PHP (a gate added during
implementation and not in the original ticket, because `--suggest`/`--fix` are themselves
gated out in that case — emitting a `match` there would describe a correction the caller
was just told is unavailable).

## Acceptance criteria

- ADR 0003's status accurately reflects that `match` exists, with its original objection
  carried forward as the verification requirement rather than discarded.
- `CONTEXT.md` has a `match` glossary entry covering the three null causes, the
  `--suggest` gate, and the embedded-PHP suppression.
- No source behaviour changes — this is a documentation-only ticket.
close_reason: Merged to develop; ADR 0003 narrowed to a verification requirement and CONTEXT.md gained a match glossary entry.

comments.text:
# wpbg-ztf implementation report

Documentation-only ticket: amend the two documents `wpbg-lsf` (the `match` field) made
factually false. No changes under `src/`, `bin/`, or `tests/`. Files touched:
`docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md` and `CONTEXT.md`, plus this report.

## What I read before writing

- `src/findings.js` — `makeFinding()`'s doc comment and the object it returns:
  `{code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, search, match, fix}`. `match` is
  `null` unless `overrides.match` is non-null.
- `src/block-locator.js` — `resolveMatch()` and the block-tree resolution it depends on
  (`resolveItemLines()`), to see exactly what gates `null` vs. a value.
- `src/pipeline.js` — where `resolveMatch()` is called (`suggest && code ===
  'BLOCK_INVALID' && searchSpan`) and where the embedded-PHP gate is applied
  (`suggest: suggest && !hasEmbeddedPhp` at the call site that builds findings).
- `docs/adr/0002-search-is-byte-exact-or-absent.md` (read only, not edited) — the
  byte-exact-or-null honesty rule for `search`, including the per-file (not per-finding)
  fallback for the position mapping.
- `docs/adr/0006-two-workflows-fix-writes-suggest-returns.md` (read only, not edited) —
  the `--suggest`-requires-`--json` boundary, and its own aside that ADR 0003 "refuses a
  per-finding `match` field" but "its own body reopens the question," instructing a
  reader to treat 0003 as a record of obstacles rather than a live prohibition. I did not
  edit 0006; this report just notes that it already anticipated the direction 0003 needed
  to move in.
- `.out-of-scope/agent-output-in-human-report.md` (read only) — why `match` has no
  human-report rendering, and the prior `wpbg-n9u` attempt that was reverted after it was
  found unreachable from any CLI invocation.

## Task 1 — `docs/adr/0003-no-corrected-markup-in-findings.md`

I did not just flip the status to "superseded." I used the advisor to check this
specifically, and it flagged that "superseded" is the wrong word: that vocabulary means
"replaced by a later ADR," there is no later ADR, and it reads as *the prohibition was
dropped* — the outcome the brief explicitly said not to write. I used instead:

> `prohibition narrowed to a verification requirement 2026-09-12 (wpbg-lsf shipped
> `match`; see Amendment below)`

I also retitled the H1 from "Findings do not carry corrected markup" (now literally
false — `match` is exactly that) to **"Corrected markup in a finding must be verified,
or absent"**, on the advisor's observation that ADR 0002's title stayed true after its
own amendment (`search` is still byte-exact-or-absent), but 0003's original title does
not survive its own amendment the same way, and a reader skimming `docs/adr/` only sees
the title. I did **not** rename the file — `0006` and `.out-of-scope/` reference it by
path, and I was told not to touch either.

The new "Amendment (2026-09-12)" section at the end of the file:
- States plainly that `match` exists and that the old title's flat "no" is no longer
  true.
- Reframes the ADR's real argument: the objection was never "corrected markup must never
  appear," it was that an *unverified* correction is a liability because a consumer
  applying it unattended can't distinguish a real fix from a guess — the same honesty
  principle ADR 0002 states for `search`.
- Cites what `resolveMatch()` actually does: splices the candidate back into the block's
  own delimiters and re-validates the *whole* candidate from scratch, returning `null`
  wherever that re-validation isn't clean.
- States the surviving rule as a binding constraint on any future producer of `match`
  (explicitly including any extension past today's leaf-only ceiling, which I named as
  `wpbg-hdl` per the code comment in `block-locator.js`, not as "a spike is open" per the
  brief's phrasing — the advisor flagged that a concurrent agent owns `wpbg-hdl` and I
  shouldn't assert an outcome for it either way): corrected markup may appear in a finding
  only after independent re-validation; a computed-but-unverified correction must be
  discarded to `null`.

## Task 2 — `CONTEXT.md`

Two changes:

1. **Fixed the `Finding` entry's tuple**, which the advisor caught and the brief didn't
   mention: it read `{code, severity, line, message, search, fix}`, missing `file`,
   `blockName`, and `match` — all of which `makeFinding()` actually returns. Updated to
   `{code, severity, file, line, blockName, message, search, match, fix}`.

2. **Added a `match` entry**, placed immediately after `search` (companion field, same
   style). It covers, as rules a consumer obeys rather than mechanism:
   - **The null causes**, honestly grouped rather than forced into exactly three (the
     brief said "three distinct meanings"; the advisor pointed out `resolveMatch()`
     actually has more return paths than that — no `save()`-compatible correction,
     re-parse producing other than one block, splice failing re-validation — and that
     "not `BLOCK_INVALID`" / "has children" / "no verified correction exists" cover them
     honestly without pretending there are only three code paths). I also added a fourth
     cause the brief's three didn't cover and that the advisor caught: `match` is gated
     on `searchSpan` in `pipeline.js`, and `search`'s own position-mapping fallback is
     per-file, not per-finding (ADR 0002) — so one unmappable item in a file leaves
     `match: null` for every block-runner finding in that file, not just the one with the
     bad mapping.
   - **`--suggest`-only**: a plain run has `match: null` on every finding.
   - **Embedded-PHP suppression**: `match: null` throughout such a file because
     `--suggest`/`--fix` are themselves declined for it.
   - **JSON-only, no human rendering, phrased as a decision**: pointed at
     `.out-of-scope/agent-output-in-human-report.md` and ADR 0006 rather than describing
     it as a gap.
   - `_Avoid_: Suggestion` — the advisor flagged this as the highest-value confusion to
     head off: `Suggestion` is a separate existing glossary term for the whole
     canonicalized file returned instead of writing, and conflating it with `match` (one
     block's replacement text inside one finding) is a live risk given how similar they
     sound. Also `_Avoid_: fix` (already avoided under `Canonicalization` for the same
     reason), `correction`, `patch`.
   - Kept the entry free of implementation detail per the domain-modeling skill
     (`resolveMatch`, `shallowMarkup`, `validateMarkup`, `summary.blocks === 1` etc. stay
     in the ADR, not the glossary).

## Where the brief was imprecise (verified against source, not trusted)

- "Three distinct meanings of `match: null`" — `resolveMatch()` actually has more return
  paths than three when read at the code level (children present; `fixMarkup` returns
  null; re-parsed candidate isn't exactly one block; splice's `validateMarkup` fails or
  isn't clean or reports more than zero items). I kept the glossary entry to the
  consumer-relevant *groupings* the brief asked for, plus the fourth cause the brief
  missed (the per-file `search`-mapping fallback), rather than asserting an exact count
  the code doesn't actually have.
- "A spike is open on whether [leaf-only] is permanent" — the code's own comment in
  `block-locator.js` says nested-parent support is "out of scope here (wpbg-hdl)," not
  that a spike is open. I named `wpbg-hdl` without asserting its outcome, since a
  concurrent agent owns that ticket.
- The brief's suggested ADR treatment ("flip to superseded") would have been wrong
  wording had I followed it literally; I used "prohibition narrowed to a verification
  requirement" instead, per advisor review.
